rawContent: Thank you @KittyWenham and @the__chez - #metoo and solidarity from here

A really important thread by a dear colleague - a call to all of us to have some sensitivity, solidarity and respect for survivors of abuse and to ensure they have the time, space and support to deal with the horrors of their experience for which they are not to blame #metoo

We speak but aren’t believed; we’re silent and feel ashamed. We live under the shadow of something carried out by someone else - isn’t it time to say enough #metoo #TimesUp and know what that really means
#DearProfessorFord We have your back #metoo #Timesup

My heart aches for every woman who has ever had to live with the horror of sexual assault, who has been shamed into silence by the shackles of power and for those who have spoken bravely only to be disbelieved #metoo

My heart aches for every single woman who has carried the weight of the abuse perpetrated against her for years, who in watching today’s world, feels that weight grow heavier, who knows exactly why she has not been able to come forward, even though the pain never goes away #metoo

Any body who thinks this is about politics has clearly NEVER been abused. This is women’s lives we’re talking about and the ONLY way it’s connected to politics is that in today’s world they are both about an ABUSE OF POWER #metoo #KavanaughFord #TimesUpKavanaugh

Gaslighting is a typical strategy of people who abuse. It - and hearing about other’s experiences of assault - can be triggering to survivors of abuse. Be kind to yourself; know you’re not alone; find something restorative and if poss go offline #metoo #KavanaughConfirmation
Survivor not victim. ‘If putting someone else’s feelings before your own experience feels uncomfortable, remember: survivors do it every day’ - thank you @LenMandy #metoo⁠ ⁠
Shamed into silence - it's taken many years to articulate my #metoo experiences. Thank you @Poynter for helping me find my voice and working with me to support others  https://t.co/ZkwEI11j2r

I strongly believe that #metoo needs to be #ustoo and we must work together as an industry to create a culture where people of all genders and generations feel safe, and where leaders lead from the top https://t.co/JQmVOBiXuv

It's taken a long time to find the courage to share my sexual assault experiences. I hope this might help others navigate the dangers of our industry and call attention to countless #metoo moments that need all of us - #wetoo - as a solution https://t.co/ZkwEI11j2r
It’s not fiction unfortunately, it’s very much real life but thought you might be interested in reading this @cynan1975 and @VanessaGebbie in light of our conversations https://t.co/ZkwEI11j2r #metoo

And I have too Kiran; too too many stories and it feels so sad that we are so often forced into silence by powerful people and that even when we bare our soul after years of silence, we do so wondering what and who next? #metoo
Thanks for retweeting my piece @spj_tweets #metoo

Sexual abuse is about power; it’s about shaming people into silence and those who are marginalised are often most vulnerable. If we feel safe to speak out, then let’s. But until we realise #metoo is actually #ustoo and we all have a role to play, the shame and silence will remain

My piece took almost 6 months to write and 13 years to gain the courage to put pen to paper. This past year was tough for me and many others who have their #metoo experiences; so if you are privileged enough to able to offer solidarity for survivors and they welcome it pls do

After I was assaulted, I briefly considered leaving journalism. But this is a profession I remain passionate about. It's one where we have a responsibility to shine a light...Shamed into silence: my #metoo story @Poynter  https://t.co/ZkwEI11j2r
Because culture change is what is needed if we are to be better allies for survivors and to show that #metoo also means #ustoo. Thank you @Poynter for leading on this
Yes #metoo

A week ago I chose to publicly share my #metoo story, one of the hardest things I've done. I wanted to use my position to shed a light on one of the scourges of #journalism, to show others they are not alone and try to wake our industry to the abuses going on

On #WorldMentalHealthDay, I’m grateful I’m not alone but still sad about the stigma around mental health. Dealing with belated, related trauma of abuse and world events have made this year tricky for me and my heart is with everyone who’s found the journey tough going #metoo

but until we tackle the stigmas that society builds around mental health and stop judging those who experience it, which is many many more than most of us probably realise, people are going to continue to suffer in silence. #mentalhealth #metoo

@YEPBusiness @SayftyCom @kalia_shreya @Alexandria_SZ This is important; much of the narrative recently has been driving division between genders & generations. This is about dismantling the power structures that have allowed abuse to pervade - ustoo I’d like to think we can call it as well as  #MeToo

As MPs wake up to the normality of sexual abuse facing women and girls, here’s my piece for @prospect_uk about speaking with my daughter about the threat and reality of gendered harassment #metoo https://t.co/enZ4thbuQ6

Sexual abuse is about power; until we dismantle the vestiges of power that lie in the hands of a privileged white macho system, the vulnerable are going to continue to be silenced and this abuse will continue. #metoo

So angry about @Telegraph #injunction story. It's a devastating blow to #PressFreedom and reaffirms that sexual abuse is about power and men who want to buy silence do so supported by systems that perpetuate white male privilege. My heart hurts for those affected by this #metoo

After years of being shamed into silence, I understand the systems that perpetuate sexual harassment and abuse and can help support those who want to change their work culture to combat them #metoo https://t.co/x3rVuCp3u0

What @AshleighRaper has done is so brave. Our industry is failing women journalists who are often shamed into silence or blamed if they speak. It’s time media leaders took decisive action to support those at risk and change the culture that enables this abuse #metoo #timesup

Because women who bravely report the abuse they have suffered haven’t got enough crap to deal with. Twisting incidents like this will only deeper the divisions that critics of #metoo, perpetrators and those protecting perpetrators want to see - you’re so right @nakedvix

It’s been a real privilege to work on this important piece on the media and #metoo and particular thanks to @ProSyn for publishing this to coincide with @NewsXchange where this has been part of conversation #NX18 https://t.co/hJzppvZO4P
